We combine technical delivery with deep connections across the energy planning ecosystem, including system operators, utilities, regulators, consultancies, research institutions, open-source communities, non-profits and funders.

items.title: A mission-driven non-profit
items.body:
OET is an independent non-profit organisation. Our objective is to strengthen the open planning commons and expand access to high-quality energy planning tools.

We are not seeking to maximise licence revenue or create dependence on proprietary systems.

items.label: Ecosystem
items.title: Connected across the energy planning ecosystem
items.body:
OET works with system operators, utilities, regulators, consultancies, universities, software maintainers, civil-society organisations and funders.

These relationships help us identify genuine gaps, avoid duplicating existing work, assemble strong partnerships and connect shared infrastructure to institutions that can use it.

items.label: Infrastructure
items.title: From shared infrastructure to real adoption
items.body: We combine software development, modelling, data, deployment and institutional capacity building. This allows us to connect investment in shared tools directly to their use in real planning processes.

items.title: A team of more than 50 specialists
items.body:
Our team includes experts in energy modelling, software engineering, data infrastructure and institutional implementation.

OET team members co-maintain PyPSA, PyPSA-Eur and other tools in the PyPSA ecosystem, as well as other energy system models such as OSeMOSYS and Calliope.

items.label: Support
items.title: Local ownership and long-term sustainability
items.body: We work with local institutions, universities, consultants and technical experts so that capability remains in the region after the programme ends.

items.label: Reusability
items.title: Reusable public value
items.body: Our programmes aim to leave behind maintained software, stronger data infrastructure, trained institutions and methods that can be reused across organisations and countries.

approach.title: We begin by identifying the systemic barrier to better planning and the institutions best positioned to create wider change.
paragraphs: We then bring together the relevant combination of planning institutions, technical communities, local partners, consultants, non-profits and funders. Programmes may combine shared software and data development with keystone deployments, training and long-term support.
OET can lead technical demanding early work, but the long-term objective is for institutions, consultants and regional experts to sustain and expand adoption without OET becoming the bottleneck.
